title: Orca lineage retry, cleanup order, plan-edit and validate lows, reader guard selection

tasks.grade_reason: worktree visibility and cleanup of every plan run through Orca
tasks.objective: Backlog topics plugin-flow-5-followups, workflow-slim-followups and policy-followups-leftovers (docs/plans/backlog.md), in scripts/factory-pipeline.py. (1) The `orca worktree set` call that `dispatch --phase lead` prints right after `git worktree add` runs before Orca knows the worktree and sets nothing; make the printed commands wait for (bounded retry) or check that `orca worktree list` shows the worktree before `orca worktree set`, and say what happens when it never appears. (2) Cleanup order: `orca terminal close --terminal <handle>` of a finished task lead returned runtime_error, and `orca worktree rm` deleted the branch asynchronously a few seconds later, so a `git branch -d` right after it failed with 'used by worktree'. The cleanup guidance and commands that `cleanup` prints must wait for the worktree record to go before deleting the branch. (3) With concise `worker-list` rows (Orca without --full), a worker released through `terminalState` but without `state` is still counted in the 'settledness not checked' note: count it as released. Read the current code first: some of this may already be fixed; report what was. Cases in tests/pipeline.test.sh with fake orca stubs only. Changelog fragment changelog.d/flow-lows-2-orca.md (### Fixed). CI runs on Linux: no test may depend on host tools of this Windows machine. The machine is short on memory: run one test command at a time with -j 1; stop your own test run before you report.
acceptance: the printed lead commands do not run orca worktree set before Orca lists the worktree
cleanup does not delete a branch before its worktree record is gone
a concise worker row released through terminalState counts as released

tasks.grade_reason: plan editing and validation used by every run lead, and the case reach of the pipeline suite
